source_review.notes: Reviewed current LevelDB Bloom implementation, table-format and usage documentation; current RocksDB Bloom/prefix documentation and maintainer format note; Dayan-Athanassoulis-Idreos's primary TODS paper from a coauthor host; and current Cassandra filter configuration. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Product configurations and measured notes remain scoped to their implementations.

evidence: Checked m bits, n distinct represented elements, k probes, bits/item b, per-candidate probability p_i, and policy-position notation.
Checked represented file membership, final database visibility, true/false positive, true negative, and forbidden false negative are distinct.
Checked whole-key/prefix domain, applicability, validity, candidate selection, metadata I/O, authoritative read, and cache metrics are separate.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Probabilistic statements consistently retain independent uniform-hash and workload assumptions.

evidence: Recomputed 10 bits/key,k=7 as approximate p=0.0081937 and 8 bits/key,k=6 as p=0.0215771.
Recomputed six independent candidates at p=0.0215771: expected false-positive probes 0.12946 and at-least-one probability 0.12268.
Recomputed model bit positions and confirmed beta checks two filters/one run while absent mu checks three filters, reads one false-positive run, and skips two.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite deterministic educational hashes are not assessed against the ideal random-hash approximation.

evidence: Re-derived zero-bit probability exp(-kn/m), false-positive approximation (1-exp(-kn/m))^k, and ideal real k=(m/n)ln2.
Verified every inserted item reuses identical transformation/probes and all its bits remain set, establishing no false negatives under intact ordinary Bloom assumptions.
Verified replacing a valid negative with source pruning and all other outcomes with authoritative lookup refines the unfiltered read result.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Policy serialization, corruption, and domain compatibility are explicit premises of the no-false-negative argument.

evidence: Reviewed empty/small/duplicate sets, bit/probe bounds, hash/seed drift, internal-vs-user keys, tombstones, merge operands, range deletions, prefix/short/cross-prefix/reverse/total-order queries.

Reviewed corrupt/truncated bits and offsets, unknown policy, checksum/I/O failure, wrong partition mapping, stale cache/file generation, comparator/extractor migration, decompression/resource limits, and adversarial collisions.

Reviewed full/block/partitioned cache cliffs, positive-heavy and range workloads, per-level allocation, rolling upgrades, canary bypass, remote storage, telemetry privacy, and false-negative response.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable model excludes serialization, failures, versions, prefixes, caching, I/O, and migration.

evidence: Each run's filter is built from every run key with the exact positions function used for lookup.
The model exhaustively checks all nine inserted run keys remain positive before evaluating lookup behavior.
Exact outputs check run/filter dimensions, beta true-positive path, mu false-positive path, reads saved/incurred, and aggregate validity.
invariant_checking.notes: Set-based bits and weak deterministic hashes make the run explanatory, not production filter evidence.

evidence: Reviewed no-false-negative proof from complete domain insertion through identical policy serialization/query and monotone bit setting.
Reviewed lookup refinement from independent candidate selection through validity/applicability, safe negative pruning, authoritative positives/fallback, snapshot resolution, and file pinning.
Reviewed tuning/evidence from explicit probability/cost assumptions through ground-truth instrumentation, steady-state experiments, zero-false-negative gates, and rollback.
proof_review.notes: The proof does not claim cryptographic hashing, adversarial guarantees, or correctness of a concrete SSTable filter implementation.

evidence: No-false-negative, lookup refinement, and tuning/evidence structures are separately labeled.
Configured/approximated/observed p, filter membership, database visibility, and end-to-end latency remain distinct claims.
Source reachability, successful model run, checksum, and vendor metrics are not generalized into universal safety or performance.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Unknown/corrupt/inapplicable filter outcomes explicitly become authoritative fallback or error, never absence.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact fifteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It reproduced all-member positivity, beta in two filter checks/one read, and absent mu in three checks/one false-positive read/two skips.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local structure/link checks passed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production hash/layout, serialized filter, SSTable, versions/tombstones, prefix query, corruption/fault, cache, file/device I/O, migration, adversarial test, or performance benchmark was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter makes the asymmetric safety contract central: compatible intact negatives can prune one represented source, while positives and uncertainty require authoritative lookup. It integrates filters after LSM candidate selection and before version resolution.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed domain/policy identity, builder self-check, whole/prefix applicability, full/block/partitioned layouts, parser/checksum/cache identity, safe fallback, tombstone/range-deletion scope, level-aware allocation, metrics, canary bypass, migration, and fault tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review states the safe branch; the finite model contrasts a true positive with a false-positive miss; derivation and ten examples connect theory to integration failures; five exercises provide complete read, format, prefix, and audit designs.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/maintainer-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Dayan, Athanassoulis, Idreos, Google, LevelDB, RocksDB, Cassandra, database, storage-engine, probabilistic-data-structure, security, reliability, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production Bloom implementation, serialized policy/filter, prefix applicability code, SSTable integration, corruption fallback, cache safety, rolling migration, adversarial resilience, realized false-positive rate, certification, nor deployment fitness.
